## Line 173

**Source:** [stdlib/geometry/spatial-structures.library.plato, line 173](../../../../../stdlib/geometry/spatial-structures.library.plato#L173).

```plato

    //==
    // # Kd-tree queries
    //
    // The `ISpatialIndex2D` / `ISpatialIndex3D` and `INearestNeighbor2D` /
    // `INearestNeighbor3D` obligations of `spatial-structures.types.plato`.
    //
    // The range query descends the tree, visiting a child only when the query box
    // reaches across the splitting plane into that child's half-space. Like every
    // traversal in the spatial package it is written as an expression: a `var` is
    // evaluated whether or not its branch is taken, so binding the recursion would
    // throw away the pruning.
    //
    // The k-nearest search is a RANK SELECTION over the stored points, not a tree
    // descent. A correct branch-and-bound descent needs a running k-th-best bound —
    // mutable state carried across a traversal — which this vocabulary has no way to
    // express, and an incorrect descent is worse than a slow correct one. Rank
    // selection costs O(n^2 + k n) against the descent's O(k log n); it is a
    // reference body, and a backend is free to substitute a real descent. The
    // worklist entry is plato-321.

    //==
    // # KdTree2D — range queries

    // The permutation holds every point exactly once.
    ItemCount(self: KdTree2D): Integer
        => self.PointIndices.Count;
```

## Line 548

**Source:** [stdlib/geometry/spatial-structures.library.plato, line 548](../../../../../stdlib/geometry/spatial-structures.library.plato#L548).

```plato

    //==
    // # Hierarchy queries — BVHs, quadtrees and octrees
    //
    // The `ISpatialIndex2D` / `ISpatialIndex3D` obligations of the hierarchies in
    // `spatial-structures.types.plato`, and the `IRaycast3D` obligation of
    // `Bvh3D`.
    //
    // Every traversal is written as a recursion over node indices, because the depth
    // is a property of the data rather than of the type and this vocabulary has no
    // loop. The recursion is the whole benefit of the structure: a node whose bounds
    // miss the query prunes its entire subtree, so the cost is the size of the
    // answer plus the boundary of the query region, not the size of the index.
    //
    // The empty result is spelled `Take(0)` on the structure's own permutation
    // array. That is not a workaround for a missing empty-array literal so much as
    // the one spelling that fixes the element type without naming it.

    //==
    // # Bvh2D

    // The leaf-order permutation holds every primitive exactly once.
    ItemCount(self: Bvh2D): Integer
        => self.PrimitiveIndices.Count;
```

    //==
    // # Quadtree2D
    //
    // Four consecutive children from FirstChild, or -1 for a leaf. A region tree
    // stores items at the node that contains them, so an internal node can carry
    // items of its own and its range is always emitted, not only at leaves.

    // The permutation holds every item exactly once.
    ItemCount(self: Quadtree2D): Integer
        => self.ItemIndices.Count;
```

    //==
    // # Octree3D and LooseOctree3D
    //
    // Eight consecutive children, otherwise identical to the quadtree. A loose
    // octree differs only in how its bounds were SIZED when it was built — the
    // stored node bounds are already the enlarged ones — so its query is the
    // inner octree's query unchanged.

    // The permutation holds every item exactly once.
    ItemCount(self: Octree3D): Integer
        => self.ItemIndices.Count;
```
